From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@metrify.com>

Cc: Metrify SRE <sre@metrify.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Mar 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Realtime inference hang during load test — urgent

Hi Marissa,

We hit a hard stop during our full-throughput cutover rehearsal. Around 13:58 PT when we pushed to 500 req/s with streaming enabled, a large fraction of requests enter a state where the server sends the first few chunks and then the connection goes silent for 20–40s. Clients then reconnect in a tight loop and many attempts result in 502s or truncated responses.

This is happening across multiple regions but most reproducible against the us-west endpoint. We captured a few traces (attached) — you'll see repeated "WS_SEND_TIMEOUT" entries and a pattern of one GPU shard reporting backpressure while others continue.

This is blocking our production cutover (was scheduled for tomorrow morning). We need a short-term mitigation and an ETA on a root-cause fix. Happy to jump on a call right now.

Attachments: ws_trace_20270321.log (text/plain), chunk_headers_capture.json (application/json)

—Elaine

Hi Elaine — thanks for the heads up and the logs.

We're escalating to SRE and the runtime team now (cc'd). I can host a short war room immediately to triage. Two quick asks while we convene:
- Can you confirm whether you were using our streaming/default or the "chunked" client in your harness?
- If possible, pause the cutover rehearsal for now so we don't spin up more traffic.

Immediate mitigation options we can try during the call:
- Switch active traffic to the non-streaming (single-response) endpoint for the next 2–4h.
- Route your traffic to a model variant in a different pool/region (should avoid the shard contention pattern).
- Temporarily reduce concurrency per connection (client-side backoff).

I'll set up a meeting and loop in Tessa for customer communications.

Subject: Fwd: Realtime inference hang during load test — set war room + triage notes

Forwarding Elaine's traces. Initial read (quick triage):
- Symptoms: partial chunk delivery followed by long silence, client reconnect loops; pattern concentrated on a subset of GPU shards.
- Preliminary log hint: repeated socket send timeouts on shard writer threads; concurrent KV cache eviction spikes at the same time window.

Proposed immediate actions (short-lived):
1) Route Metrify traffic to the 'compat-1' model variant in a different pool (US-EAST) — avoids the problematic shard routing. (Logan)
2) Increase websocket send timeout and socket buffer sizes for the impacted pool by +3s and +25% respectively. (Dev)
3) Disable aggressive KV eviction policy for the pool for the next 6 hours to see if contention drops. (Grace)
4) Tessa to coordinate comms and confirm when Metrify switches to non-streaming if they elect to. (Tessa)

I've attached the raw traces to this thread and created a tracking ticket INFR-8923. Let's pick owners and target a rollback window after the fix.

Attachments: ws_trace_20270321.log, chunk_headers_capture.json

—Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 21 Mar 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Realtime inference hang during load test — set war room + triage notes

Quick technical update from triage:
- Reproduced locally against a similar load profile. The runtime shows a per-shard writer queue draining while the shard's eviction thread obtains a global mutex to move KV entries; during prolonged eviction the writer goroutines block on socket sends because internal batching expects timely writes. The result is many sockets in a transient backoff followed by reconnects.
- This looks like a coordination deadlock between eviction and the write path when shard load is skewed. Not a network device issue.

Immediate fixes I will push now (targeted, reversible):
- Increase io_write_timeout to 5s for pool-id us-west-2a.
- Bump socket send buffer (SO_SNDBUF) by 25% for the pool.
- Flip KV eviction from adaptive -> passive for the pool (stop background compaction).

I'll instrument an extra metric (shard_writer_block_ms) and add a short-lived alert at 500ms. If we see improvement in 20m we'll leave the config for the next 6h and plan a code change to decouple eviction from writer path (INFR-8923).

Logs and the temporary config patch are pushed to the drive link: https://drive.redwood/example/metrify/ws-traces/20270321

—Dev
Dev Patel
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 21 Mar 2027 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Realtime inference hang during load test — urgent (update)

Elaine — thank you for your patience. Quick summary of actions taken and current status: 

What we did (15:10–15:40 PT):
- Routed Metrify traffic for the rehearsal to the compat-1 variant in us-east (avoided the overloaded shard pool).
- Applied temporary config changes in us-west pool: increased websocket write timeout, increased socket buffer, and disabled aggressive KV eviction.
- Added a short-lived metric and alert to monitor shard writer blocking.

Observed result: within ~12 minutes after the changes we observed a >90% reduction in WS_SEND_TIMEOUTs in the affected pool and the reconnect loop frequency dropped to near-zero for the test harness. Your team reported that the client-side reconnect loop stopped.

Next steps / timeline:
- Short-term (next 24–48h): keep the temporary config in place while we run extended soak tests.
- Medium-term (1 week): runtime team will ship a code fix to decouple eviction from the write path and add safer backpressure handling (tracked in INFR-8923).
- We will provide a postmortem and regression test case by next Tue.

If you'd like, we can keep the compat-1 route active until your production cutover is complete. I understand this is late notice; we've also escalated to VP of Product to discuss any credit/contract accommodations for the disruption.

Attachments referenced: ws_trace_20270321.log, chunk_headers_capture.json

Thanks again — we're monitoring and will keep you updated hourly while the soak runs.

Best,
